questions.question:
**Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.**

He has painted that picture so often that he can do it with his (eyes closed).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** "No improvement". **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence implies that the artist is so familiar with the painting that he doesn't need to see it to recreate it.
 
• The phrase **"with his eyes closed" **is a figure of speech that suggests he could do it easily without actively looking, based on his experience and expertise.
 
• **Taking a look at the proposed alternatives:**
 
 
• "With his arms full" would imply physical constraint or challenge which doesn't seem to match the context here.
 
• "With his eyes opened" is the normal state for painting and doesn't convey the idea of effortlessness or mastery.
 
• "With his mind blank" might suggest the ability to perform tasks from muscle memory, but it lacks the connotation of mastery conveyed by "eyes closed".
 
 
 
• So after analyzing all the options, it can be concluded that no improvement is needed in the phrase **"with his eyes closed" **as it accurately communicates the intended meaning.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 4". **

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

P - When the game of life is finally over there is no second chance to correct our errors.

Q - Time is the greater equalizer of all mankind.

R - Time offers opportunity but demands a sense of regard.

S - It has taken away the best and the worst of us without regard of either.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **QSRP**

Q is the first sentence, followed by S which tells us how time is the greater equalizer of mankind.

Then comes R, followed by P which talks about how time offers opportunity in demand for something.

Hence, the correct combination is QSRP, as seen in **Option 1.**

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

Little knowledge of playing volleyball (1)/ that she possessed proved to be (2)/helpful at the time of an inaugural match. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The error is in **Part 1 **of the sentence.

**Little** means **‘something that is small in size, amount or degree.’**

It is generally used with the definite article, ‘the’, to signify something that is much, such as knowledge.

Hence, the correct answer is:

**‘The little knowledge of playing volleyball that she possessed proved to be helpful at the time of an inaugural match.’**

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

I had not completed my English homework (1)/ so I thought I was done with when the (2)/ teacher asked me to hand it in. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The error is in **Part 2 **of the sentence.

The phrasal verb **‘done with’** means **‘something that is useful’**.

The correct phrasal verb to be used in the sentence is **‘done for’**, meaning **‘a situation so bad that is impossible to get out of’**.

The correct sentence is:

**‘I had not completed my English homework so I thought I was done for when the teacher asked me to hand it in.’**

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Active/Passive voice. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active voice.**

He saw him conducting the seminar on personality development.

options.text: He was seen by me to conduct the seminar on personality development.
He was seen conducting the seminar on personality development.
He saw the seminar on personality development being conducted by him.
He saw the seminar on personality development to be conducted by him.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **‘He was seen conducting the seminar on personality development.****’**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Let's understand this we the below example and rule-application:
 
• When there are **two** objects in an active sentence, there are **two possible active sentences and two possible passive sentences.**
 
• **Sentence 1**: *The professor gave the students the books.*
 
• **Sentence 2:** *The professor gave the books to the students.*
 
• There are two objects in each of the above sentences:
 
 
• **Object 1** = indirect object → the students
 
• **Object 2** = direct object → the books
 
 
 
• An indirect object is very often a person, a direct object a thing. When a direct object is followed by an indirect one, we put ***to*** in front of the indirect object.
 
• **Active sentence 1: "**The professor **(sub) + **gave **(verb) + **the students **(indirect object) + **the books **(direct object)"**
 
• Active sentence 2: "The professor (sub) + gave (verb) + the book (direct object) + to the students (indirect object)"
 
• Each of the objects (books/students) in the active sentences can become a subject in the passive sentence.
 
• **Passive sentence 1 (Personal Passive): "**The students **(sub) + **were given **(verb) + **the books **(object) **(by the professor) **(by-agent)**"
 
• Passive sentence 2: The books (sub) + were given (verb) + to the students (object) (by the professor) (by-agent)

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech.**

Rashmi said to me, "Where is the telephone exchange"?

options.text: Rashmi asked me that where the telephone exchange was.
Rashmi asked me where the telephone exchange was.
Rashmi asked me where was the telephone exchange.
Rashmi wanted to know where the telephone exchange was.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **‘Rashmi asked me where the telephone exchange was’.**

Sentence 1 uses an unnecessary ‘that’, making the sentence incorrect.

Sentence 3 keeps the reported speech in the form of a question, while Sentence 4 uses ‘wanted to know’ instead of ‘asked’, making it incorrect.

Only Sentence 2 keeps the correct structure and reporting verb and changes the interrogative form in the reported speech, making it the correct choice.
